A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same INPO research work. Their main text, equations, tables, and Appendices A–B are readable and support a reliable comparison.

before.justification: v1 reports original INPO evaluations on three alignment benchmarks and six academic benchmarks, plus a KL-regularization ablation.

after.justification: v3 reports original benchmark evaluations and ablations, including additional experiments initialized from LLaMA-3-8B-Instruct in Appendix B.

M1.justification: Algorithm 1 retains the same OMD update, pairwise squared loss, current-policy sampling, and final-iterate output. The tournament selection details in v3 Section 4.1 already appear in v1 Appendix B. The new convergence analysis does not replace the experimental procedure.

E1.justification: Both versions use the same training prompt collections, three alignment benchmarks, and six academic benchmarks. Appendix B adds an instruction-tuned model initialization, which changes the model configuration rather than dataset or task coverage.

E2.justification: v3 adds evaluated SPPO comparisons to both the main alignment and academic benchmark tables while retaining the existing comparators. This substantively strengthens comparison against general-preference methods: v1 cited SPPO as the closest related work but did not report its performance.

E3.justification: Appendix B changes the reported eta from 0.0075 to 0.005, retaining tau = eta/3, and adds experiments initialized from LLaMA-3-8B-Instruct. Average response length is no longer reported. The principal benchmark metrics, judges, three training iterations, and eight-response sampling remain unchanged.

E4.justification: The KL-with/without ablation remains, but v3 removes its response-length measurements and associated length-control analysis. Appendix B adds an examination of whether alignment gains persist when training starts from an already instruction-tuned checkpoint.

E5.justification: Neither version reports experimental seed counts, repeated-run uncertainty, confidence intervals, or significance tests. The expanded tables retain point-estimate reporting.

E6.justification: Many scores are replaced: Table 1 INPO (PM) changes from 41.5/38.3/8.35 to 42.6/37.8/8.43 on AlpacaEval/Arena-Hard/MT-Bench. The academic GPQA comparison reverses from INPO 30.5 versus SFT 27.8 to 28.9 versus 30.2. SPPO rows and Appendix B Tables 4–5 are added, while response-length results disappear. Changed hyperparameters and incompletely explained score revisions prevent interpreting these as same-setting performance gains.

T1.justification: Assumption A changes from bounded negative log reference probability to bounded log-density ratios along feasible iterates. Lemma 2 and Theorem 3 replace reference entropy with D = max KL(pi || pi1), with corresponding proof revisions. New Theorem 4 and Appendix A.3 establish last-iterate contraction and an O(1/T) KL bound using eta_t = tau(t+2)/2.

C1.justification: v3 adds last-iterate convergence as an explicit theoretical contribution and broadens its empirical superiority claim from iterative DPO to online RLHF methods including SPPO. The abstract and introduction remove the earlier contribution claim concerning KL regularization for response-length control.

C2.justification: The explanation for academic benchmark gains changes from the small training-prompt budget to better use of pretrained knowledge and abilities. Appendix B attributes smaller gains from instruction-tuned initialization to prior RLHF limiting further improvement. The response-length-control interpretation is withdrawn; finite-sample analysis remains future work.

D1.justification: Appendix B adds SPPO implementation-source information and the instruction-tuned checkpoint reference, and revises the documented eta selection. Section 4.1 explicitly identifies other LLM comparison scores as copied from Dong et al. Existing scheduler, warm-up, batch-size, and tournament details are retained.

R1.justification: v3 adds Tang et al. (2024) to motivate online rather than offline alignment and expands discussion contrasting current-policy sampling with prior geometric-mixture approaches. The existing game-theoretic positioning and core related-work coverage remain largely unchanged; SPPO was already cited in v1.

P1.justification: v3 locally rewrites the preliminaries and algorithm exposition, replaces the detailed Online IPO subsection, swaps the academic-results and ablation subsections, and moves tournament details into the main text. Appendix B gains separate implementation and results paragraphs. The title and overall six-section structure remain intact.

P2.justification: v3 adds two appendix tables and SPPO rows in retained benchmark tables, removes parenthetical response-length entries, and updates captions and highlighting. The academic and ablation tables exchange order. The table style and single-column layout remain substantially unchanged; neither version contains figures.

improvement.justification: v3 substantially strengthens the theoretical foundation through revised assumptions and initialization-dependent regret bounds, plus last-iterate analysis where v1 justified only the averaged policy. Evaluating SPPO, the closest general-preference competitor, also addresses an important comparative gap. The new convergence rate requires a varying eta, unlike the reported fixed experimental setting; unexplained score revisions and removed length diagnostics limit verification. Nevertheless, the stronger foundational analysis and direct comparative evidence constitute a substantial overall improvement.
